claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The baseline alloy exhibits a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons are examples of the stated as-deposited initial state.
Controlled high-energy ball milling or rapid thermal processing can induce structural disorder or partial amorphization and create nanoscale features in the alloy.
The nanostructuring treatment can be implemented without compromising overall mechanical stability.
Nanostructuring produces nanoscale grain boundaries and structurally disordered regions.
The induced grain boundaries and structural disorder modify the local energy landscape and reduce transition-associated pinning sites.
Disruption of long-range order lowers the nucleation barrier for the magnetostructural phase change.
A lower nucleation barrier produces a smoother, more temperature-spread phase transition.
Broadening the phase transition reduces thermal and magnetic hysteresis.
Nanostructuring increases surface-to-volume ratio and may thereby accelerate heat exchange.
Excessive transition broadening or amorphization may diminish the magnetocaloric entropy change.
Relative to the as-deposited control, the nanostructured alloy will have reduced thermal or magnetic hysteresis width during low-field cycling.
Relative to the as-deposited control, the nanostructured alloy will show improved cycle reversibility.
The nanostructured alloy will retain its peak magnetocaloric entropy change or show only a moderate reduction.
The baseline material has limited heat-exchange kinetics because of its bulk form.
The predictions apply to similar non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type compositions under low applied fields and within the operational temperature range of previous studies.
The predictions require an optimized nanostructuring level that does not excessively degrade the magnetocaloric peak or mechanical stability.
XRD and TEM can be used to quantify grain size and the degree of structural disorder in treated and control samples.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant hysteresis reduction, or loss of entropy change beyond an acceptable limit, would falsify the combined hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state includes melt-spun microribbons, but the baseline attributes limited heat exchange to the material's bulk nature; microribbons are not straightforwardly a bulk geometry and ordinarily have a higher surface-to-volume ratio than ingots.

Arc-melted ingots and melt-spun ribbons are labeled 'as-deposited,' although these are distinct fabrication states and arc melting is not ordinarily a deposition process, leaving the baseline state internally ambiguous.
